clue.text: Figure boy keeping vermin should be turned over

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the assembled letters are read backwards
the boy keeps, or holds, the vermin within himself, so one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: A lad who keeps rats and mice ought to be reported to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a verb meaning reckon; here it is a noun, a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal is a kind of number written with a point, so it is a figure.

clue.text: Spy novelist?

definitions.meaning: One of the Cambridge spies who defected to Moscow
Anthony ... wrote A Clockwork Orange

explanation.definitionFit: Two famous Britons share the surname: a Soviet double agent and the author of A Clockwork Orange.

clue.text: British in war, heads spinning, as indoctrinated

indicators.note: heads spinning are whirled about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: In wartime the British were dizzy with propaganda and so were indoctrinated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' reads as the leaders of the war effort, but it is just fodder; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be brainwashed is to have beliefs forced on you by persistent pressure, which is what indoctrinated means.

clue.text: Sound of lamb being eaten by mamba, appalling!

indicators.note: the letters sit swallowed inside the run of words that follows, as prey inside a snake

explanation.surface: A lamb being swallowed by a mamba is a horrible sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of 'mamba' and the start of 'appalling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleat is the noise a lamb makes, conventionally written as this word.

clue.text: Character a shade to the left, to the left of river

indicators.note: placed on the left means written before the next piece
in an across entry, going to the left means reading right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Describing a person: a bit of a left-winger, living left of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a shade' looks political after 'to the left', but it is a colour; the river is the Yorkshire Ure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's nature is their essential character or temperament.

clue.text: Whole shape altering, or triangle

indicators.note: a change of shape reorganises the figure, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Geometry talk: a whole figure whose form changes, or perhaps a triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shape altering' rearranges TRIANGLE; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral can mean complete or entire, forming a whole, as in an integral part.

clue.text: One to twelve are there unceasingly

definitions.meaning: the numbers one to twelve are arranged in a circle on a clock face
without stopping, all day and all night

explanation.definitionFit: Working twenty-four hours without a break is an idiom for doing something continuously, without ceasing.

clue.text: Line on meeting so exchanged with acquaintance at last?

definitions.text: Line on meeting so exchanged with acquaintance at last?

indicators.note: the letters swap places with one another, so they come out in a fresh order
at last points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The remark traded on bumping into an old acquaintance after a long gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: it is what one says on meeting an acquaintance again at last.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the informal greeting used to someone you have not met for ages.

clue.text: Creative process isn't restricted by blip?

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ping is a short blip of sound, as on a radar or sonar
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A creative endeavour that is not held back by a minor setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blip' suggests a minor setback; here it is the sound a radar makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing a picture with paints is a creative activity, an artistic process.

clue.text: Religious image encapsulating northern arboretum

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing as in a capsule, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pieta is a picture or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ

explanation.surface: A devotional statue set within a tree garden in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinetum is a plantation of pine trees, a specialised arboretum; this is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Result of burning wood

definitions.meaning: the powdery residue left after a fire
the timber of a common tree, used for tool handles

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the residue left after combustion and the hardwood timber of a familiar tree.

clue.text: A slight crawler has to remain loyal to faction?

definitions.meaning: a thin twig-like insect that creeps slowly

definitions.text: has to remain loyal to faction?
definitions.meaning: read playfully, this is someone who must stay inside a sect

explanation.definitionFit: The name is a long thin insect resembling a twig, and read as a phrase it suggests staying put in a sect.

clue.text: Fashion era is rubbish

parts.note: garb is clothing, a style of dress or fashion

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing a whole era of fashion as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is waste or refuse, a synonym for rubbish, also used of nonsense.

clue.text: Inspector feeding passport, say, back into car close to border

indicators.note: one piece is fed into the other, so it sits inside it
going back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a passport is an example of identification, abbreviated ID

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A border official sliding a passport back into a car near the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ID into DI, which goes 'into' AUTO, and R (from 'close to border') ends it; 'feeding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines accounts officially, so is a kind of inspector.

clue.text: Entering plunge, every bomb starts to explode

indicators.note: the letters enter, or go inside, the other word

parts.note: to dunk is to plunge something into liquid

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Every bomb dropped into the water starts to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' picks E and B, which go inside DUNK. 'explode' means discredit, as in exploding a myth.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk an idea is to expose it as false, as one might explode a myth.

clue.text: Ship that goes under a vessel?

definitions.meaning: a vessel that trades along the shore
a mat placed beneath a glass or cup, a vessel for drink

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small coastal trading vessel and a mat put beneath a drinking glass.

clue.text: Possible case involving children in clubs, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a lawsuit about minors
in bridge, clubs and diamonds are the lower-ranking pair of card groups

explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, clubs and diamonds are the lower-scoring suits; read literally the phrase is a legal action about children.

clue.text: Head or heart of a writer?

definitions.meaning: to head something is to go in front or guide it
the graphite core of a pencil, a writing tool

explanation.definitionFit: To be at the front, guiding others, is one sense; the graphite core of a pencil is the other.

clue.text: Delayed sniggers concealed here?

definitions.meaning: late, in arrears
people hide a snigger behind a raised palm

explanation.definitionFit: The word means late or in arrears, and a stifled laugh is hidden behind a raised palm.

clue.text: Female astronaut circling globe's first to see mountain's contour

indicators.note: to circle something is to surround it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Sally Ride was the first American woman in space

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A woman in orbit circling the Earth, the first to see the shape of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts G (picked by 'globe's first') inside RIDE; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow crest of high ground, a feature of mountains.

clue.text: Amber changing before green light in stoppage of traffic

indicators.note: placed before means written first in the answer
changing alters the letters into a different order

explanation.surface: A traffic light changing from amber to green, just before traffic stops.
explanation.walkthrough: The traffic-light picture is all surface: amber is fodder, and 'stoppage of traffic' means a trade ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade, a stoppage of commercial traffic.

clue.text: Classic performance to satisfy houses lacking a shade?

indicators.note: a word that houses another holds it inside

parts.note: to slake a thirst is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: A classic show that pleases homes which are without a lampshade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests a lampshade; here it means colour, so lacking it is pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet is a classic of the repertoire, performed constantly.

clue.text: A US woman eclipsing rival before end of election, very tough

indicators.note: to eclipse something is to cover it, so the woman encloses the rest

parts.note: dame is American slang for a woman
an anti is an opponent, someone set against you, so a rival

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An American woman outshining her rival before the end of an election proves very tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipsing' reads as outshining, but it means covering; 'anti' as a noun is an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine means hard as diamond, unbreakable, and so extremely tough.

clue.text: Cousin he abandoned before daughter given support

indicators.note: placed before means written first
abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A cousin walked out before his daughter got any help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as the cousin walking out, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushioned means padded or softened, given support against impact.

clue.text: Precisely two hits

explanation.surface: An exact pair of strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang means exactly, as in slap-bang in the middle.

clue.text: Not this nor that one goes in lower

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: nether means lower, as in nether regions
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A choice refused: this one is lower than that.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not the one and not the other of two.

clue.text: Water, traditionally, that's in a kettle

definitions.meaning: in classical thought water was one of earth, air, fire and water
the heating coil inside an electric kettle

explanation.definitionFit: Water was one of the four classical building blocks of matter, and a kettle's heating coil goes by the same word.

clue.text: Content in business

definitions.meaning: the substance or subject of a text
an affair or concern

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the substance of something written and an affair or concern.

clue.text: Examine a shell

explanation.surface: Inspect a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A testa is the hard outer coat of a seed, a botanical shell.

clue.text: Vegetable in ship beginning to open up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ark is a ship, as Noah's

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Greens in a boat's hold, starting to be opened.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' turns the whole run of ship plus first letter backwards; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a green pod vegetable, also called ladies' fingers.
